title: Three-Week IB Spanish Ab Initio Revision Plan
summary: IB Spanish ab initio revision plan for November: organise three focused weeks of writing, reading, listening, topic triage, timed practice, and rest.
body_markdown:
This **IB Spanish ab initio revision plan** gives November candidates a three-week route through writing, reading, listening, vocabulary, and timed practice. Allow 35-60 minutes on most days, with longer sessions for simulations and correction. Start by diagnosing weaknesses, spend the second week applying language, and use the final week to rehearse and recover.


Three weeks can feel both long and impossibly short. There is time to improve, but revision becomes more useful when you decide what deserves attention first.


The assessment includes Paper 1 writing and Paper 2 receptive skills, with separate listening and reading sections. Your school manages the individual oral separately, so confirm whether it is complete before allocating revision time to it.


### The three-week plan at a glance


Week Main priority Evidence to produce


One Diagnose weaknesses and rebuild essential language Error log, theme ranking, corrected writing


Two Apply Spanish through exam-style tasks Timed mini-sections, listening corrections, text-type checklists


Three Rehearse and protect energy Timed simulations, final corrections, recall sheets


Throughout the plan, prioritise weak areas, produce Spanish regularly, mark practice, and revisit errors within 48 hours. Protect sleep and your other subjects’ study time.


The[RevisionDojo Spanish ab initio resource hub](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ib/ib-spanish-ab-initio) brings together Questionbank, Study Notes, Flashcards, AI Chat, grading tools, Predicted Papers, Mock Exams, Coursework Library, and Tutors. Choose the resource that addresses your next task; you do not need to use everything.


### Week one: diagnose before you revise


Begin with one short reading task, one listening task, and one writing prompt under light time pressure. Select questions from the[Spanish ab initio Questionbank](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ib/ib-spanish-ab-initio/questionbank) , then mark your responses before deciding what to study.


Sort mistakes into four categories:


- **Knowledge:** missing vocabulary or grammar.
- **Recognition:** familiar language you did not identify quickly.
- **Technique:** misunderstanding instructions, audience, purpose, or question wording.
- **Timing:** incomplete or rushed answers.


Each category suggests a different repair. Missing vocabulary needs retrieval practice; familiar words missed in audio need focused listening. Learning another word list will not solve every problem.


### Rank the five themes


Rate your confidence across identities, experiences, human ingenuity, social organization, and sharing the planet. Mark each red, amber, or green, using your diagnostic results as evidence.


For red themes, build compact clusters of nouns, verbs, adjectives, opinions, and examples. For amber themes, retrieve language without notes. For green themes, answer questions to check that confidence matches performance.


Connect vocabulary rather than collecting isolated words. A health cluster might combine food, exercise, stress, advice, and future intentions, giving you language you can adapt across tasks.


Complete two writing sessions: one with notes, then one without. Use the[Spanish ab initio course guide](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/complete-guide-to-ib-spanish-ab-initio-course-details-assessment-tips-and-faqs) to review assessment expectations. Check audience, register, structure, and common language errors.


A manageable session is 15 minutes of retrieval, 25 minutes of practice, and 10 minutes of correction. On busy days, use a 20-minute maintenance session.


A student calmly gives Spanish revision its turn while textbooks for other subjects wait in line


### Week two: turn knowledge into performance


Alternate writing, listening, reading, and grammar across weekdays. Finish with a timed mini-section, then reserve weekend time for correction and a longer practice session.


### Make writing more reliable


Choose three text types from your course materials. Create a checklist for opening, closing, audience, tone, paragraphing, and purpose. Practise these conventions in shorter responses before attempting another complete paper.


Focus grammar work on frequent errors: agreement, verb formation, tense consistency, articles, negatives, and prepositions. Rewrite sentences from your own work so each correction addresses a demonstrated weakness.


The[guide to achieving a 7 in Spanish ab initio](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/how-to-get-a-7-in-ib-spanish-ab-initio) provides broader preparation advice. Use Flashcards for recall and AI Chat to investigate confusing phrases, checking uncertain explanations against teacher guidance and course materials.


### Listen and read actively


For listening practice, use three passes:


- Identify context, speakers, purpose, and overall meaning.
- Answer detailed questions, watching for numbers, negatives, and changing opinions.
- Replay difficult sections, consult an available transcript, and record missed language.


This is a revision method; follow the prescribed playback arrangements during simulations and examinations.


For reading, track names, dates, opinions, and contrast words such as *pero* , *aunque* , and *sin embargo* . Locate evidence for each answer instead of translating every sentence.


Finish with a 30-40 minute set using[RevisionDojo Test Builder and Exam Mode](https://www.revisiondojo.com/features/test-builder) . Review whether mistakes came from language gaps or rushing.


### Week three: rehearse, correct, then reduce


Complete one timed writing simulation and one receptive-skills simulation early in the week. Use school-supplied examination materials or suitable Predicted Papers and[RevisionDojo Mock Exams](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/revisiondojo-mock-exams) . Follow the applicable examination timing and instructions.


Mark every uncertain answer, including correct guesses. For writing, combine grading tools with teacher feedback to identify recurring problems. Rewrite the weakest paragraph, then check whether the correction transfers to a fresh task.


Use this flexible sequence:


- **Seven to five days before:** complete simulations and begin corrections.
- **Four to three days before:** repair recurring errors and practise weak themes.
- **Two days before:** retrieve vocabulary and do light listening.
- **One day before:** review briefly, check equipment, and finish early.


Move sessions around other examinations. A short Spanish retrieval session can preserve continuity when another subject needs your largest study block. The advice on[building speed with timed IB practice](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/timed-ib-practice-tests-17-proven-ways-to-boost-exam-stamina-and-speed) can help if timing remains difficult.


### Finish with a plan you can sustain


Keep a lighter evening each week and maintain regular sleep. If confusion persists, bring your error log and marked responses to a RevisionDojo Tutor for focused guidance.


Three weeks can sharpen your decisions. Use RevisionDojo to diagnose, practise, correct, and rehearse, then arrive rested enough to use what you know.
